scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Jerk appeared in the United States in the early 1960s.
It gained momentum through a series of hit singles in 1964, including tracks by The Larks, The Miracles, and The Contours.
By the late 1960s, the dance had reached France, where it was adopted by pop artists and became a staple of the era's music scene.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The Jerk was a popular social fad dance, performed in clubs and social settings during the 1960s.
It is a secular dance intended for entertainment and social participation.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Down And Dirty: The Contemporary Versions Of The Great All Time Dances! [Full VHS] (https://archive.org/details/down-and-dirty-the-contemporary-versions-of-the-great-all-time-dances-full-vhs)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The Jerk is performed individually.
The dancer holds their hands at face level, crossing the wrists in front of the chest before sweeping them outward.
This outward sweep occurs on the first count of the music, creating a jerky, sudden motion.
Watch for The Jerk Sweep.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Individual, non-partnered.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is primarily associated with 1960s rhythm and blues, though it later incorporated psychedelic music.
Early tracks were typically recorded with standard band instrumentation of the era.
The pulse is 4/4.
Upbeat rhythm and blues characterized by a driving, danceable pulse suitable for sudden, jerky movements.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Cross wrists in front of the chest.
Step 2: Sweep arms outward on count 1.
Drill: Practice crossing wrists at chest level.
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); repetitions per step: about 4
Counts on screen

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Snap fingers on the first and third counts of the hand motion.
Step 4: Move hips and legs in rhythm with the arm sweeps.
Drill: Time the outward push to the beat.
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Add finger snaps on counts 1 and 3.
on_screen: Split screen: front view / back view
Tempo label changes: slow → half → full
